question_html: In considering the qualitative aspects of the entity's accounting practices, the auditor may become aware of possible bias in management's judgements. The auditor may conclude that:

options.A: Indicators of possible management bias always constitute misstatements for the purpose of drawing conclusions on individual accounting estimates
options.B: Management bias in making accounting estimates is entirely irrelevant to forming an opinion on the financial statements as a whole
options.C: The cumulative effect of a lack of neutrality, together with the effect of uncorrected misstatements, causes the financial statements as a whole to be materially misstated

question_html: The term 'fair presentation framework' is used to refer to a financial reporting framework that requires compliance with the framework's requirements and:

options.A: Prohibits management from ever providing any disclosure beyond those specifically required by the framework, under any circumstances
options.B: Never contains any acknowledgement regarding fair presentation, since fair presentation is solely the auditor's responsibility, not management's
options.C: Acknowledges explicitly or implicitly that it may be necessary for management to provide disclosures beyond those specifically required by the framework, or acknowledges explicitly that departure from a requirement may be necessary to achieve fair presentation (expected only in extremely rare circumstances)
options.D: Applies exclusively to financial statements prepared under Ind AS, and to no other financial reporting framework

answer_html:
C. Acknowledges explicitly or implicitly that it may be necessary for management to provide disclosures beyond those specifically required by the framework, or acknowledges explicitly that departure from a requirement may be necessary to achieve fair presentation (expected only in extremely rare circumstances)

A 'fair presentation framework' requires compliance with its requirements and additionally acknowledges (explicitly or implicitly) that additional disclosures beyond those specifically required may be necessary, or acknowledges that departure from a requirement may (in extremely rare circumstances) be necessary, to achieve fair presentation; a 'compliance framework' requires compliance but contains neither acknowledgement.

question_html: 'General purpose financial statements' are financial statements prepared in accordance with a 'general purpose framework', which is best described as:

options.A: A financial reporting framework designed exclusively for the internal use of the entity's own management, and not intended for any external user
options.B: A financial reporting framework that applies only to listed entities, and never to unlisted entities
options.C: A financial reporting framework that is entirely unrelated to the concepts of fair presentation or compliance

question_html: Before the commencement of the audit, the joint auditors should discuss and develop a joint audit plan, which includes identifying division of audit areas and common audit areas; the joint auditors should also:

options.A: Each obtain a separate, mutually inconsistent management representation letter from the entity, without any coordination among themselves
options.B: Refrain from communicating with each other at any stage, so as to preserve each firm's independent judgement
options.C: Divide the audit report itself into as many separately bound volumes as there are joint auditors, even where they agree on the opinion
options.D: Obtain a common engagement letter and a common management representation letter

answer_html:
D. Obtain a common engagement letter and a common management representation letter

As part of joint audit planning, the joint auditors obtain a common engagement letter and a common management representation letter, in addition to jointly establishing the overall audit strategy and developing the joint audit plan.

question_html: While each joint auditor is responsible only for the work allocated to them (including proper execution of the audit procedures for that allocated work), all the joint auditors are jointly and severally responsible for:

options.A: The audit work not divided among the joint auditors and carried out by all of them, decisions taken by all the joint auditors in respect of common audit areas, and ensuring that the audit report complies with the requirements of the relevant statutes and applicable Standards on Auditing
options.B: Only the work specifically allocated to each individual joint auditor, with no residual joint responsibility of any kind
options.C: Only matters that resulted in a qualified opinion, to the exclusion of matters resulting in an unmodified opinion
options.D: Only the fee-sharing arrangement agreed among the joint auditors, with no responsibility for the audit work itself

answer_html:
A. The audit work not divided among the joint auditors and carried out by all of them, decisions taken by all the joint auditors in respect of common audit areas, and ensuring that the audit report complies with the requirements of the relevant statutes and applicable Standards on Auditing

Joint auditors are jointly and severally responsible for undivided audit work carried out by all of them, decisions on common audit areas, matters agreed among them, compliance of the financial statements/report with relevant statutes and applicable SAs, and related matters - while each is individually responsible only for their own allocated work.

question_html: Under section 143(1) of the Companies Act, 2013, the auditor is required to inquire into certain matters, including:

options.A: Whether the company's competitors have complied with similar statutory provisions, regardless of the company being audited
options.B: Whether loans and advances made by the company on the basis of security have been properly secured and whether the terms are prejudicial to the interests of the company or its members, and whether personal expenses have been charged to revenue account

options.A: Only the total remuneration paid to the company's directors during the year, with no reference to information/explanations or books of account
options.B: Only the market capitalisation of the company as at the balance sheet date

question_html: As per section 143(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 read with Rule 13 of the Companies (Audit and Auditors) Rules, 2014, if the auditor has reason to believe that a fraud involving an amount of Rs. 1 crore or above is being or has been committed in the company by its officers or employees, the auditor shall:

options.A: Report the matter to the Central Government within such time and in such manner as prescribed
options.B: Report the matter only to the company's competitors, so as to warn the industry at large
options.C: Take no reporting action whatsoever, since fraud reporting is entirely voluntary at the auditor's discretion
options.D: Report the matter exclusively to the company's shareholders in the annual general meeting, bypassing the Central Government entirely

answer_html:
A. Report the matter to the Central Government within such time and in such manner as prescribed

For a fraud involving Rs. 1 crore or above, the auditor reports the matter to the Central Government within the prescribed time and manner; for a fraud below that threshold, the auditor reports to the Audit Committee (or the Board, in other cases) instead.

subject: Auditing and Ethics
case_facts_html: CA Priyanka Vashisht is the statutory auditor of Emberton Foundries Ltd., a company to which CARO 2020 applies, for the year ended 31st March, 2026. During the audit, she notes: (i) the company was sanctioned cash credit limits of Rs. 7 crores from a nationalised bank on the security of its current assets, of which Rs. 2 crores were used to fund the purchase of a long-term capital asset; and (ii) the company raised funds through a preferential allotment of equity shares during the year but has not utilised the entire amount for the disclosed purpose stated in the relevant board resolution.
question_html: Having identified both matters as reportable exceptions under CARO 2020, what must CA Priyanka Vashisht additionally do in her CARO report, as per Paragraph 4?

options.A: Simply mark both answers as 'qualified' without providing any further basis or explanation
options.B: Omit any further explanation, since Paragraph 4 of CARO 2020 applies only to favourable answers and not to qualified ones
options.C: Refer both matters directly to the National Financial Reporting Authority instead of stating any basis in her own report
options.D: State the basis for the unfavourable or qualified answer given in respect of each of these matters

answer_html:
D. State the basis for the unfavourable or qualified answer given in respect of each of these matters

Paragraph 4 of CARO 2020 requires that where the answer to any Paragraph 3 matter is unfavourable or qualified, the auditor's report shall also state the basis for such unfavourable or qualified answer.
